We are asking you to be in a research study by Columbia University. The study is titled "political beliefs and attitudes" (IRB-AAAV1276). When all your questions have been answered, you can decide if you want to be in the study or not. This process is called ‘informed consent.’


PURPOSE

The purpose of this survey is to understand people’s social and political beliefs and attitudes.


COMPENSATION

This will take about 2 minutes. You will receive $0.40 for your participation in this study today.


PROCEDURES

Your participation is completely voluntary, and you do not have to participate if you don't want to. If at any point you wish to stop your participation, you are free to do so without any repercussions for your relationship with the researchers or the institution. If you agree to participate in the study, you will be asked a series of simple questions about your views of the world. Specifically, you will be asked some questions about your views regarding social and political issues. Then, you will be asked a series of demographic questions. You are free to skip any or all questions you do not wish to complete. Your responses are and will remain completely anonymous.


BENEFITS, RISKS, STRESS, OR DISCOMFORT

There are no foreseeable risks to taking part in this study. However, there is always the possibility that you may be offended by something in the survey, and you are allowed to choose to skip questions if they make you uncomfortable. You may or may not receive personal (direct) benefit from taking part in this study. The possible benefits of taking part in this study include gaining further insight into your own views, beliefs, and attitudes as well as gaining insight into how contemporary research is being conducted. In addition, the information collected from this research may help others in the future, as well as expand the scientific knowledge on the topic, and we hope society will benefit from the knowledge gained. Of course, you may choose not to take part in this research study. In such a case, you may exit this survey at any point. 


CONFIDENTIALITY

Every effort will be made to keep your personal information confidential. However, we cannot guarantee total privacy. The data collected will be given a code number and separated from any information that could identify you. We will not ask you to provide any identifying information, such as your legal name. The research file that links your name to the code number will be kept in a password protected computer and only the Principal Investigator and the study staff will be able to see this file. If information from this study is published or presented at scientific meetings, your name and other personal information about you will not be used.


CONTACT INFORMATION

If at any time you have questions regarding the research or your participation, you should contact the investigator, Dean Baltiansky, who will answer all questions. You can reach him by email: dab2257@gsb.columbia.edu. You should also contact the investigator or a member of the research staff if you have any concerns or complaints about the research.
